summary: Mentor can now tell you in simple words what each update brings, and its version reads like a date.
Mentor Settings has an Updates tab: every update this Mentor had, and Ask Mentor to go over one with you.
Mentor now warns you and asks first before it restarts to install an update.
In Mentor Settings, Updates, the list of updates is sorted by year and month.
Mentor Settings now uses the whole width of the window, like the Recipes app.
When something does not work as expected, you can tell Mentor's maker: right-click the desktop, Report a problem.
A shorter desktop menu, and the bell's suggestions now have their own tab in Mentor Settings.
In the Recipes app, switching a recipe off only switches it off, and a widget's switch works at once.
Every card in the chat can now be talked about, update cards no longer pop up, and switching a recipe off asks first.
Mentor Settings is back in the desktop menu, next to Settings, and the menu now stays exactly as it is.
Mentor Settings has its own icon: the Mentor owl.
Mentor's self-check now also makes sure Mentor keeps getting its updates.
The bell now has More buttons for more GitHub projects, apps and news, from more sources. History shows the question each answer was for.
The gear now turns while Mentor works on your request, and the bell opens narrow when it has no cards.
Make the chat's text larger or smaller with Ctrl and the mouse wheel (or Ctrl + + − 0); the cards widen with it, and Mentor remembers the size.
Mouse-look now works in 3D games: Mentor switches to a game mouse by itself while a game is in front. The Recipes app can delete a recipe.
Mentor now tells you in the chat when a program crashes, and full system upgrades are safer: fresh signing keys first, a free-space check, and a check of the start-up files.
No more false warning after your computer sleeps: Mentor's own checks no longer look broken when Windows pauses Mentor.
Settings no longer freezes after Mouse & Touchpad, about 37 languages can be chosen in Settings, and the assistant's text box always stays in view.
The setup screens show the simpler Mentor owl.
Copy text from anything on the screen with Shift+Super+T, reminders in the chat, websites as apps of their own, and games set up when you ask.
Maximizing Mentor's window or making it full screen no longer shows everything small for a moment.
Mentor follows your Windows time zone, and you can approve its password questions with Windows Hello (with the new Mentor program on Windows).
Your laptop's volume keys, Windows' volume and Mentor's volume are now one and the same (with the newest Mentor program on Windows).
Your laptop's volume keys, Windows' volume and Mentor's volume are one and the same, one step per key press (with the newest Mentor program on Windows).
Small fixes: zooming the chat works right after a start, cards no longer hide under the Super+Z box, and copying text from the screen is more reliable.
More small fixes: problem reports leave out passwords written in words, recipe checks list every command, and fewer false alarms in the logs.
Changing your password is easier: Mentor Settings opens a simple window for it instead of a text window.
Clearer recipe checks: the list of what a recipe would run is complete and holds only commands.
Chromium and apps open smoothly: no empty terms window the first time, and the assistant can open them with every engine.
The assistant recovers from its own small mistakes: when it asks a tool for something in the wrong form, it is told and tries again, instead of stopping in the middle of your request.

Recipes and web apps with Greek names each get a file of their own, undoing a change that is not there no longer asks for your password, and the assistant keeps going when its engine says something unexpected.
Mentor in other languages: with the desktop in Greek its self-check no longer reports a problem that is not there, and your folders keep their names so Mentor keeps finding your recipes.

Quieter in the background: a big text file in Downloads no longer keeps Mentor busy, a program that crashes again and again gives one card, and a broken download of an update is simply tried again later.
One Update button: when you press Update in Mentor Settings, the update card in the chat shows it too, and the other way round; and only the newest update has a card.
No false alarm without a Windows host: Mentor started on its own no longer reports the shared clipboard as broken, and its self-check names an error by the error itself.
The assistant knows the new Mentor window on Windows: one Start over button, and the screen switches in one row.
Lighter with many tabs open: Chromium puts tabs you have not looked at for a while to sleep, and when memory runs short Mentor first compresses what is idle instead of closing a program.
Smooth animations: windows, the overview and menus open and close smoothly again, drawn by the graphics card; with the Graphics card switch off they stay off.
Answers you can read over any page: when you ask with the box over a program (Super+Z), the answer has a solid background and the page behind no longer shows through.
Alt+Shift switches between your keyboard languages, as on Windows; shortcuts with Alt+Shift in them keep working.
The assistant knows the newest Mentor program on Windows: the mouse caught only in full screen, and what changed for slow starts.
Pick calm window colors in Mentor Settings: 20 dark and light sets. The taskbar and the system menus follow them too.
Window buttons are now small yellow, green and red squares, and light or dark always matches your window colors.
Mentor Settings has a Themes tab: accent colors and your pointer's color and size. Mentor also warns before a restart that would stop the assistant.
Pressing Space on a big file in Files now shows at once that its preview is opening. Two small fixes in the chat and Mentor Settings.
Dragging around a picture's preview or History no longer moves the desktop: it stays still.
News cards say plainly what they do: Skip article brings the next news, and Don't show news from a site stops only that site. Not now waits one day.
With dark window colors, programs such as Bitwarden now open dark too.
Copying your key on NVIDIA's page brings Mentor back with the key already in the box. Folders in Show Apps show every app in their picture.
The box for a new key stays open while you get the key from another program, until you press Save or Cancel.
No more two pointers at a larger zoom: while the zoom would make it too large, the pointer is one size smaller.
At a larger zoom, the pointer's Size slider in Mentor Settings shows only the sizes that look different.
With light window colors, the line under each open app on the taskbar is dark, so it can be seen.
Screenshots copied on Windows now paste into web pages at any size, without the page freezing.
The green, yellow and red cards in the chat are nearly solid now, so they can be read over any wallpaper.

A guard against harmful programs: a watch for unusual programs, a card when an unknown program goes online (Mentor Settings, Security), no programs from temporary folders, and a weekly check of this system's programs.
Show Apps and the search take the tones of your window colors, light or dark. OpenSnitch's own window is no longer listed among the apps.
OpenCode and other programs that unpack a part of themselves into a temporary folder start again.
When a part of Mentor stays broken, Mentor offers to tell its maker (Report a problem), so that an update can fix it.
A menu after each picture: a smaller copy, a copy as PNG, JPG or WebP, the text in it, save, edit.
Two pictures in a row no longer leave two menus open.
Programs from Flathub, such as Google Chrome, get Mentor's colored window buttons and window colors.
History opens in a window of its own: minimize, maximize and close, like any program.
